subject: Deployment isolation + MAP: performance stress plan & findings

Subject: MAP kickoff: isolation + perf stress plan for hosted/dedicated/private comparisons

Hi Alexa —

Great to meet last week. Per our call, attached is a focused MAP deliverable outlining the perf stress plan we propose to run against a representative workload from Oneta. Primary goals: validate latency/TTFT at target concurrency, quantify throughput scaling, and exercise autoscaler behavior across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes so your SRE team can confirm isolation guarantees for regulated traffic.

High-level schedule (attached sheet has detail):
- May 18: Share sample workload + client-side load harness (Oneta provides 2k user prompts)
- May 19–20: Baseline runs (hosted) to capture steady-state and cold-starts
- May 21: Dedicated pool runs (reserved capacity) to capture tail behavior under noisy neighbor test
- May 22: Private (customer infra) runs with CloudOps to validate autoscaling ramp and network effects
- May 24: Joint review (30m) and decision on pilot/PO next steps

Action: can you confirm the workload file transfer by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks —
Tessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: isolation_stress_plan.xlsx (xlsx)

Alexa —

Quick answers:
- Private connectivity: we'll provide a temporary deployable test agent (container) and an ephemeral API key scoped to the eval resources. We'll need a single bastion IP/SSH user or short-lived ingress rule for the agent. Details in the attachment (isolation_stress_plan.xlsx).
- Dedicated noisy-neighbor: yes — our perf harness supports synthetic background tenants and tail-latency injection to reproduce contention. We will run three classes of injections: CPU-bound, memory-pressure, and KV-cache eviction bursts.

Preliminary test matrix (summary):
- Metrics: TTFT (time-to-first-token), P50/P95/P99 latency to first token, per-request total completion, requests/sec throughput, tokens/sec, and per-second tail variance.
- Concurrency targets: 1–256 reqs in steps (1, 8, 32, 64, 128, 256) with fixed prompt lengths (avg 480 tokens).
- Autoscale tests: step ramp (x1 -> x4 over 5m) and burst ramp (x1 -> x8 in 60s).

We'll run the hosted baseline first and attach raw CSVs (ramp_results.csv).

Marissa
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Alexa Chen <alexa@oneta.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark results: hosted / dedicated / private — quick summary (raw attached)

Team — attaching the raw PDFs/CSVs (benchmark_results_q1.pdf + ramp_results.csv). Below are sanitized highlights from today's runs — we focused on steady-state at average prompt length 480 tokens and a tail stress ramp. Numbers are median/P95 unless noted.

Hosted (multi-tenant) — baseline
- TTFT: 78ms median; P95 220ms
- Per-request latency (end-to-end): P50 110ms; P95 285ms; P99 420ms
- Throughput: stable at 95 reqs/sec at concurrency 64; tokens/sec ~45k
- Notes: autoscale reacted in ~45–60s to 4x ramp, occasional P99 spikes during external platform maintenance window.

Dedicated (reserved pool) — reserved GPUs
- TTFT: 52ms median; P95 98ms
- Per-request latency: P50 64ms; P95 120ms; P99 160ms
- Throughput: 320 reqs/sec at concurrency 256; tokens/sec ~160k
- Notes: very low variance, noisy-neighbor injection caused less than 5% tail uplift when synthetic tenants saturated CPU-bound ops.

Private (Oneta on-prem, this run) — customer infra, agent-in-VPC
- TTFT: 92ms median; P95 240ms
- Per-request latency: P50 100ms; P95 275ms; P99 530ms
- Throughput: 200 reqs/sec at concurrency 128; tokens/sec ~90k
- Notes: autoscale ramp was slower (averaged ~110s to add nodes given k8s HPA conservative CPU thresholds). Network egress variance added to tail during bursting. When we pre-warmed KV cache, tail improved ~15%.

Interpretation / recommendation:
- If predictability and lowest tail are primary, Dedicated is the clear choice (consistent P95/P99, immediate capacity).
- For faster time-to-value and simpler ops, Hosted is reasonable but expect higher tail variability during platform events; mitigate with prefix caching and smaller batching window.
- Private is viable but requires tuning: pre-warm cache, more aggressive HPA settings or custom autoscaler, and ensuring network egress SLAs.

Next MAP steps (proposal):
1) May 25–27: Pilot config — Dedicated reserved pool (4 GPUs), run production-like traffic for 7 days.
2) May 28: Commercial terms review (Karthik to lead).
3) May 31: Exec sign-off + PO issuance once pilot meets SLA targets (P95 < 120ms at 99% availability).

I'll attach the raw CSVs (ramp_results.csv) and the summary PDF.

Marissa

Attachments: benchmark_results_q1.pdf, ramp_results.csv
